# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: daily-publish `cli` leg (build-macos.yml run 41008008179) fails in "Build macOS release" on BOTH matrix archs with `errSecInternalComponent` during CodeSign (`GoogleAppMeasurement.framework`), auto-filed as gh-1986.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Both macOS matrix arch builds die at the first codesign of the embed phase: `Fa.app/Contents/Frameworks/GoogleAppMeasurement.framework/Versions/A: errSecInternalComponent` → `Command CodeSign failed with a nonzero exit code` → `** BUILD FAILED **`.

**Root cause**: The persistent `ci-signing.keychain-db` on the self-hosted runner (fa-m5-2) had **auto-locked before the build's first codesign**. Exact chain:

1. The keychain auto-locks after ~5 min of keychain inactivity, and `security set-keychain-settings -t 0` **cannot fix it non-interactively on this host** (GUI SecurityAgent prompt — documented screenshot-confirmed in `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile`, gh-1954; in run 41008008179 the bounded attempt was killed by its own 5 s alarm: `Alarm clock: 14` in the "Provision signing" step log at 05:25:05).
2. **2026-10-29 10:24 UTC** (run 40857357741, fa-m5-2): the gh-1954 `host-signing-provision --force` roll-out **deleted and re-created** the persistent keychain (`ci-sign: --force: deleting existing keychain …/ci-signing.keychain-db for fresh re-provision`). `create-keychain` defaults restored the ~5-min auto-lock that the keychain no longer had.
3. **2026-10-30 05:25** (run 41008008179): `ci-sign install fa-macos` unlocked the (re-created, locking-default) keychain; the `-t 0` reset was alarm-killed (item 1), so the unlock was the LAST keychain access.
4. The build then compiled for **2h14m35s with zero keychain activity** (job log silent 05:44:54 → 07:39:34; the whole build issues no codesign before the embed phase), so the keychain auto-locked minutes after provisioning.
5. At **07:39:34 both concurrent matrix legs hit their first codesign** (embed phase) within 0.4 s of each other and failed with `errSecInternalComponent` on the same embedded framework — the classic locked/inaccessible-keychain signature.

**Impact**: Every `build-macos` run whose compile phase outlives the ~5-min auto-lock (i.e. every full Swift compile — 1–2.5 h) fails at the embed phase after spending the entire build window, killing the daily-publish `cli` leg until the keychain settings or unlock coverage change. The iOS lane is unaffected: gh-1954 gave gym a 60 s re-unlock watchdog.

**Why the previous green runs passed**: before the 10-29 `--force` re-provision the keychain carried an applied no-auto-lock setting (the 10-27 green run 4045520860 shows no alarm in provisioning); the re-create reset it, and the macOS lane — unlike the iOS lane — has no unlock watchdog to keep it open.

**Fix approach**: Apply the established gh-1954 doctrine ("the REAL anti-lock mechanism is the unlock watchdog; `unlock-keychain -p` never prompts") to the macOS leg: in `build-macos.yml`'s build-macos job, arm a background `ci-sign unlock` watchdog (60 s cadence) right after successful signing provisioning, covering the whole signing window (build, DMG/PKG packaging, notarize, no-sandbox build), and kill it in the `if: always()` Cleanup step (pid-file guarded, identity-checked kill). `set-keychain-settings` is deliberately left best-effort in ci-sign — it can never be relied upon on this host.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-1986 (the gh-1954 series fixed the iOS gym lane's identical failure class and introduced the keychain re-create that re-exposed the macOS lane).

- name: Provision signing via ci-sign (persistent host keychain)
        id: signing
        env:
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD }}
          CI_SIGN_P12_B64_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64
          CI_SIGN_P12_PASSWORD_ENV: MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD
          MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
            echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "✅ Signing certificate found — provisioning via ci-sign..."
            # gh-1865 model v3 (owner decision 2026-10-28): NO per-arch
            # temporary keychains, NO search-list writes, NO default-keychain
            # flips. ~/bin/ci-sign keeps the PERSISTENT ci-signing.keychain-db
            # provisioned (idempotent — concurrent matrix legs re-verify in
            # milliseconds) and pins the identity by SHA-1, so a concurrent
            # leg's same-subject certificate (gh-1865, run 40455401630)
            # cannot shadow resolution. The old per-arch keychain
            # delete+create race was gh-1852; the eviction race was gh-1866;
            # both classes are structurally gone.
            ~/bin/ci-sign install fa-macos
            CERT_SHA1=$(~/bin/ci-sign sha1 fa-macos)
            CERT_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign name fa-macos)
            echo "identity_sha1=$CERT_SHA1" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "identity_name=$CERT_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "gh-1865: signing identity pinned by SHA-1: $CERT_NAME ($CERT_SHA1)"
            echo "signed=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

          if [ -n "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$MACOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" | base64 --decode > profile.provisionprofile
            echo "profile_embedded=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # Make the profile visible to Xcode manual signing. Decoding
            # goes through ci-sign plist — the legacy CMS decoder needs a
            # default keychain, which this model never sets.
            PROFILE_UUID=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
            PROFILE_NAME=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract Name raw -)
            PROFILE_TEAM=$(~/bin/ci-sign plist profile.provisionprofile | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw - 2>/dev/null || true)
            echo "Profile: $PROFILE_NAME / UUID: $PROFILE_UUID / team: $PROFILE_TEAM"
            mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles"
            cp profile.provisionprofile "$HOME/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning Profiles/${PROFILE_UUID}.provisionprofile"
            echo "profile_uuid=$PROFILE_UUID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "profile_team=$PROFILE_TEAM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

            # gh-1865 fail-fast precheck (owner option B): the profile must
            # embed the provisioned certificate — a mismatch aborts here in
            # seconds instead of surfacing as a dead archive after the full
            # build. Skipped on unsigned runs (no provisioned cert).
            if [ -n "${CERT_SHA1:-}" ]; then
              ~/bin/ci-sign doctor profile.provisionprofile fa-macos
            fi
          else
            echo "⚠️  No provisioning profile found — TestFlight will warn"
            echo "profile_embedded=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Build macOS release (${{ matrix.arch }})

--- provisioning head:
if [ -z "$MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64" ]; then
  echo "⚠️  No signing certificate found — building unsigned (development only)"
  signed=false
  echo "signed=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
else
  signed=true
  echo "✅ Signing certificate found — provisioning via ci-sign..."
--- provisioning tail:
# the no-sandbox build; the always() Cleanup step stops it.
if [ "$signed" = "true" ]; then
  ~/bin/ci-sign unlock
  nohup bash -c 'while :; do sleep 60; ~/bin/ci-sign unlock >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done' \
    </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  disown
  echo $! > ci-sign-watchdog.pid
  echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog armed (pid $(cat ci-sign-watchdog.pid), 60s cadence — gh-1986)"
fi
--- cleanup (if: always()):
# gh-1986: stop the keychain unlock watchdog armed in the
# provisioning step — the persistent ci-signing keychain is host
# state and stays; only this job's watchdog process is per-job.
# Existence-guarded + identity-checked: a provisioning failure
# before the watchdog armed must never kill a recycled pid.
if [ -f ci-sign-watchdog.pid ]; then
  WPID="$(cat ci-sign-watchdog.pid)"
  if ps -p "$WPID" -o command= 2>/dev/null | grep -q "ci-sign unlock"; then
    kill "$WPID" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog stopped (pid $WPID)"
  else
    echo "ci-sign unlock watchdog pid $WPID no longer running — nothing to stop"
  fi
  rm -f ci-sign-watchdog.pid
fi
# gh-1865 model v3: no per-job keychain to delete — the persistent
# ci-signing keychain is host state, never removed from jobs.
rm -f certificate.p12 installer.p12

# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: daily-publish `cli` leg (build-macos.yml run 41008008179) fails in "Build macOS release" on BOTH matrix archs with `errSecInternalComponent` during CodeSign (`GoogleAppMeasurement.framework`), auto-filed as gh-1986.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Both macOS matrix arch builds die at the first codesign of the embed phase: `Fa.app/Contents/Frameworks/GoogleAppMeasurement.framework/Versions/A: errSecInternalComponent` → `Command CodeSign failed with a nonzero exit code` → `** BUILD FAILED **`.

**Root cause**: The persistent `ci-signing.keychain-db` on the self-hosted runner (fa-m5-2) had **auto-locked before the build's first codesign**. Exact chain:

1. The keychain auto-locks after ~5 min of keychain inactivity, and `security set-keychain-settings -t 0` **cannot fix it non-interactively on this host** (GUI SecurityAgent prompt — documented screenshot-confirmed in `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile`, gh-1954; in run 41008008179 the bounded attempt was killed by its own 5 s alarm: `Alarm clock: 14` in the "Provision signing" step log at 05:25:05).
2. **2026-10-29 10:24 UTC** (run 40857357741, fa-m5-2): the gh-1954 `host-signing-provision --force` roll-out **deleted and re-created** the persistent keychain (`ci-sign: --force: deleting existing keychain …/ci-signing.keychain-db for fresh re-provision`). `create-keychain` defaults restored the ~5-min auto-lock that the keychain no longer had.
3. **2026-10-30 05:25** (run 41008008179): `ci-sign install fa-macos` unlocked the (re-created, locking-default) keychain; the `-t 0` reset was alarm-killed (item 1), so the unlock was the LAST keychain access.
4. The build then compiled for **2h14m35s with zero keychain activity** (job log silent 05:44:54 → 07:39:34; the whole build issues no codesign before the embed phase), so the keychain auto-locked minutes after provisioning.
5. At **07:39:34 both concurrent matrix legs hit their first codesign** (embed phase) within 0.4 s of each other and failed with `errSecInternalComponent` on the same embedded framework — the classic locked/inaccessible-keychain signature.

The iOS lane is unaffected: gh-1954 gave gym a 60 s re-unlock watchdog.

**Fix approach**: Apply the established gh-1954 doctrine ("the REAL anti-lock mechanism is the unlock watchdog; `unlock-keychain -p` never prompts") to the macOS leg: in `build-macos.yml`'s build-macos job, arm a background `ci-sign unlock` watchdog (60 s cadence) right after successful signing provisioning, covering the whole signing window (build, DMG/PKG packaging, notarize, no-sandbox build), and kill it in the `if: always()` Cleanup step (pid-file guarded, identity-checked kill). `set-keychain-settings` is deliberately left best-effort in ci-sign — it can never be relied upon on this host.

### Root Cause

The macOS release builds died on their FIRST codesign (`GoogleAppMeasurement.framework` embed) with `errSecInternalComponent` — the locked-keychain signature. On 2026-10-29 the gh-1954 `host-signing-provision --force` roll-out re-created the persistent `ci-signing.keychain-db` on fa-m5-2, restoring the ~5-min inactivity auto-lock; `set-keychain-settings -t 0` cannot fix it non-interactively on this host (GUI SecurityAgent prompt — the bounded attempt was alarm-killed: `Alarm clock: 14` in the provisioning log). The iOS gym lane got a 60 s unlock watchdog for exactly this class in gh-1954; the macOS leg never had one.

- `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml` (build-macos job): after signing provisioning succeeds, arm a background keychain re-unlock watchdog — `ci-sign unlock` immediately + a disowned loop re-unlocking every 60 s across the whole signing window (build, DMG/PKG packaging, notarize, no-sandbox build); pid recorded in `ci-sign-watchdog.pid`; gated on `signed=true` (unsigned runs stay keychain-free). The `if: always()` Cleanup step stops it with an existence-guarded, identity-checked kill (never a recycled pid). Same mechanism gh-1954 gave the Fastfile gym lane.

- `test/ci_macos_keychain_unlock_watchdog_guard_test.dart` — 4 ACs: watchdog armed with ≤60 s cadence + `disown` (AC1); negative check — no unlock before the `signed=true` gate (AC2); `always()` Cleanup stops the same pid file, existence-guarded (AC3); the Fastfile gym-lane watchdog still stands (AC4). All PASS (RED→GREEN verified).
- Watchdog mechanics smoke-tested against a fake `ci-sign`: cadence unlocks fire, `ps` identity check matches, kill stops the loop, absent-pid path never kills.
- All 7 workflow/keychain guard test files: 49 tests passed; full `dart test` suite run recorded in the task ledger.

### Notes

- No product code changed — CI-only fix; the keychain itself remains persistent host state (gh-1865 model v3 untouched), only a per-job unlock loop was added.
